entries.answer: Trabaho means work, and it is the general word covering a job, a task and a piece of work, with the context deciding which. As a noun it is the thing you are employed to do, and maayo ang trabaho means the work is good while sayop ang trabaho means it is poorly done, so the word describes the quality of the work rather than the worker, which is a distinction a learner can miss. As a verb, trabaho means to be employed, and the phrase naa siyang trabaho means he has a job. The related terms people ask about are a job, which is a specific position with a role, and employment, which is the condition of having paid work as opposed to self-employment. In the Philippines the employer is often called the company or the firm, and a person who supervises others even informally is sometimes given the same word, so it is not strictly a word for management.
